entries.title: AC not cooling
entries.meaning: Let's find out why your AC isn't cooling the room.
aliases: how do I clean my ac filter
safety: Use a sturdy stool or ladder, not a chair, when you reach up to the indoor unit.

steps.say: Check the remote is set to cool mode, not fan, dry or auto.
steps.target: the display screen of the AC remote control

steps.say: Set the temperature a few degrees below the room temperature, and the fan speed to high.
steps.target: the display screen of the AC remote control

steps.say: Close the doors and windows, and draw the curtains if the sun comes in.
Make sure no furniture or curtains block the air going in or out of the indoor unit.
steps.target: the wall-mounted indoor AC unit and the space around it

steps.say: If it's still not cold after thirty minutes, switch the AC off with the remote and at the wall.
steps.target: the wall switch or plug that powers the AC

steps.say: Open the front cover of the indoor unit, or the front grille of a window AC.
steps.target: the front cover panel of the indoor AC unit
steps.caution: Make sure the AC is switched off at the wall first.

steps.say: Slide out the mesh air filters from behind the cover.
steps.target: the plastic mesh air filter behind the front cover of the AC

steps.say: Rinse the filters under running water, or vacuum off the dust if they're only dusty.
steps.target: the plastic mesh air filter
steps.caution: Never use hot water. A little mild soap is fine for heavy dirt.

steps.say: Let the filters dry fully in the shade, not in direct sun.
Put the dry filters back, close the cover, and switch on. Cooling can take three minutes to start.
steps.target: the front cover panel of the indoor AC unit

steps.say: Outside, check nothing blocks the outdoor unit, or the back of a window AC.
steps.target: the outdoor AC unit with the round fan grille
steps.caution: Don't reach into the fan or touch the metal fins.

steps.say: If it still isn't cooling after all this, it may need gas or a repair. Please call a technician.

remind.say: Your AC filters are due for a clean. A clean filter keeps the room cool.

entries.title: Water dripping from the AC indoor unit
entries.meaning: Let's find out why water is dripping from the indoor unit.
symptoms: water coming out of the ac
water on the floor under the ac
safety: Switch the AC off, then turn off its wall switch or breaker before you touch it.

steps.say: Water dripping from the outdoor unit or its pipe outside is normal. Only drips indoors are a problem.
Move anything water could damage from under the indoor unit, and put a bowl or towel there.
steps.target: the floor area directly under the wall-mounted indoor AC unit

steps.say: Open the front cover of the indoor unit and slide out the air filters.
steps.target: the front cover panel of the indoor AC unit
steps.caution: Use a sturdy stool or ladder, not a chair.

steps.say: Rinse the filters under running water, then let them dry fully in the shade.
steps.target: the plastic mesh air filter
steps.caution: Never use hot water on the filters.

steps.say: Put the dry filters back and close the cover.
steps.target: the front cover panel of the indoor AC unit

steps.say: Outside, find the thin drain pipe that carries water away from the indoor unit.
steps.target: the thin plastic drain pipe coming out of the wall below the indoor AC unit

steps.say: Make sure it slopes downward all the way and isn't blocked or squashed.
steps.target: the thin plastic drain pipe of the AC

steps.say: Keep the doors and windows closed while the AC runs.
Switch the AC back on. If water still drips inside, switch it off and please call a technician.

entries.title: AC remote not working
entries.meaning: Let's get your AC and its remote talking again.
safety: Keep the remote's small batteries away from young children.

steps.say: Look at the remote's screen. If it's blank or faint, the batteries are weak.
steps.target: the display screen of the AC remote control

steps.say: Take the batteries out and put them back, matching the plus and minus marks.
steps.target: the battery cover on the back of the AC remote control

steps.say: If the screen is still faint, replace both batteries with new ones of the same type.
steps.target: the battery cover on the back of the AC remote control

steps.say: Point the remote straight at the indoor unit, with nothing like a curtain in between.
steps.target: the wall-mounted indoor AC unit

steps.say: Wipe the small receiver window on the indoor unit, and make sure nothing covers it.
steps.target: the small dark signal receiver window on the front of the indoor AC unit

steps.say: Switch off nearby tube lights or neon lights, then try the remote again.
Test the remote with your phone camera. Aim it at the lens, press a button, and look for light.
steps.target: the small bulb at the front tip of the AC remote control
steps.caution: Some phones, like iPhones, can't show this light.

steps.say: If there's no light even with new batteries, the remote is faulty and needs replacing.
If the remote does light up but the AC won't respond, check the AC's breaker or wall switch is on.
steps.target: the wall switch or plug that powers the AC

steps.say: Meanwhile, you can run the AC with the small on off button on the indoor unit.
steps.target: the small on/off button on the indoor AC unit
steps.caution: Where it sits differs by model, so check your manual.

steps.say: If the AC still won't start from either one, please call a technician.

entries.title: Bad smell from the AC
entries.meaning: Let's clear out the smell coming from your AC.
safety: Switch the AC off, then turn off its wall switch or breaker.
Use a sturdy stool or ladder, not a chair, to reach the indoor unit.

steps.say: Open the front cover of the indoor unit, and slide out the air filters.
steps.target: the front cover panel of the indoor AC unit

steps.say: Wash the filters under running water to clear the dust.
steps.target: the plastic mesh air filter
steps.caution: Never use hot water on the filters.

steps.say: Let them dry completely in the shade before you put them back.
Put the filters back, close the cover, and switch the AC on again.
steps.target: the front cover panel of the indoor AC unit

steps.say: Run the AC in fan only mode for a few hours to dry out the inside.
steps.target: the display screen of the AC remote control

steps.say: Look for smells nearby, like a bin, shoes or damp clothes, and move them away from the AC.
If it still smells, the inside needs a deep clean. Please call a technician to service it.

entries.title: Check the engine oil on a bike or scooter
entries.meaning: Let's check your engine oil level, and top it up if it's low.
safety: Put the bike on its centre stand on firm, level ground.
Warm a cold engine for a few minutes, then switch it off and wait a few minutes.

steps.say: Look low on the right side of the engine for an oil window or an oil filler cap.
steps.target: the oil level window or oil filler cap low on the right side of the engine

steps.say: If there's a window, the oil should sit between the upper and lower marks next to it.
steps.target: the oil level window low on the right side of the engine

steps.say: If there's a filler cap, unscrew it and wipe the dipstick on it clean.
steps.target: the oil filler cap with a dipstick low on the right side of the engine
steps.caution: The engine and exhaust may be hot, so don't touch them.

steps.say: Rest the dipstick back in the hole without screwing it in, then pull it out again.
steps.target: the oil filler hole low on the right side of the engine

steps.say: The oil should reach between the upper and lower marks on the dipstick.
If it's at or near the lower mark, add a little oil of your manual's grade through the filler.
steps.target: the open oil filler hole low on the right side of the engine
steps.caution: Don't fill above the upper mark.

steps.say: Recheck the level, then screw the filler cap back on firmly and wipe up any spills.
steps.target: the oil filler cap low on the right side of the engine

entries.source: Honda Activa 6G OM PDF p.63-64 + Honda Shine OM PDF p.56-57 + TVS Jupiter OM PDF p.58 + Bajaj Pulsar 150 OM PDF p.28 + Royal Enfield Classic 350 OM PDF p.27; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Check and lube a motorcycle drive chain
entries.meaning: Let's check how loose your motorcycle chain is, then clean and lube it.
safety: Switch the engine off, take out the key and shift into neutral.
Put the motorcycle on its centre stand on firm, level ground.

steps.say: Find the drive chain that runs from the engine to the rear wheel.
steps.target: the drive chain running from the engine to the rear wheel sprocket
steps.caution: Some chains are fully covered. Your manual shows how to see them.

steps.say: Halfway along the chain, move it up and down with your finger and see how far it travels.
steps.target: the middle of the drive chain between the two sprockets

steps.say: That up and down movement should be within the slack range in your owner's manual.
Turn the rear wheel slowly by hand. The chain should move smoothly, with no tight or stiff spots.
steps.target: the rear wheel of the motorcycle

steps.say: Wipe the chain clean with a dry cloth while you turn the rear wheel.
steps.target: the drive chain running from the engine to the rear wheel sprocket

steps.say: Spray or drip chain lube onto the chain as you turn the wheel, then wipe off the extra.
steps.target: the drive chain running from the engine to the rear wheel sprocket
steps.caution: Use the chain lube your manual names, and keep it off the tyres and brakes.

steps.say: If the slack is outside the range or the chain is kinked, have a mechanic adjust it.

remind.say: Your bike chain is due for a clean and lube. Let's check its slack too.

entries.title: Bike or scooter won't start
entries.meaning: Let's go through the simple checks for why it won't start.
safety: Move the bike off the road and stand it on firm, level ground.

steps.say: If there's an engine stop switch on the right handlebar, make sure it's set to run.
steps.target: the engine stop switch on the right handlebar switch block

steps.say: Push the side stand fully up. Many bikes won't start with it down.
steps.target: the side stand on the left side of the bike
steps.verify: the side stand is folded up

steps.say: On a motorcycle, shift into neutral, or hold the clutch lever in.
On a scooter, squeeze a brake lever while you press the start button.
steps.target: the brake lever on the left handlebar of the scooter

steps.say: Keep the throttle closed and press start for no more than five seconds at a time.
steps.target: the start button on the right handlebar
steps.caution: Wait ten to fifteen seconds between tries to rest the battery.

steps.say: Check there's enough petrol. On older bikes, turn the fuel tap to on or reserve.
steps.target: the fuel gauge on the instrument cluster

steps.say: On older bikes with a choke, pull it on for a cold start, then off once warm.
If the lights are dim or the starter won't turn, use the kick starter if there is one.
steps.target: the folding kick start lever low on the side of the bike
steps.caution: Kick firmly from the top, and never kick while the engine is running.

steps.say: If the engine warning light stays on, or it still won't start, please call a mechanic.

entries.title: Check tyre pressure and tyre condition
entries.meaning: Let's check your tyre pressure and look the tyres over for damage.
safety: Park on firm, level ground, switch the engine off and take out the key.

steps.say: Check the pressure while the tyres are cold, before riding or after a very short ride.
Look up the right front and rear pressures in your owner's manual.
Take off the valve cap and press a tyre pressure gauge firmly onto the valve.
steps.target: the tyre valve stem on the wheel rim

steps.say: Add air until it matches your manual, then screw the valve cap back on.
steps.target: the tyre valve stem on the wheel rim

steps.say: Look around each tyre for cuts, cracks, bulges, or nails stuck in the tread.
steps.target: the tread and sidewall of the tyre

steps.say: Find the small tread wear marks. If the tread has worn down to them, the tyre needs replacing.
steps.target: the small tread wear indicator mark on the tyre sidewall

steps.say: If it's punctured, damaged, or keeps losing air, get it fixed at a tyre repair shop.
steps.caution: With a puncture, ride slowly and only as far as the nearest repair shop.

entries.title: Check brake fluid and brake lever feel
entries.meaning: Let's check the brake fluid level and how the brakes feel. Just a check, no repairs.
safety: Switch the engine off and park upright on firm, level ground with the handlebar straight.

steps.say: Find the small brake fluid window on the right handlebar, next to the front brake lever.
steps.target: the small brake fluid reservoir with a window on the right handlebar next to the front brake lever
steps.caution: Drum brakes have no fluid window. If so, skip to the lever check.

steps.say: The fluid should be above the lower or MIN mark in the window.
steps.target: the small brake fluid reservoir with a window on the right handlebar next to the front brake lever
steps.caution: Don't open the cap. Brake fluid damages paint and plastic.

steps.say: If the rear brake is a disc, check its fluid level on the right side the same way.
steps.target: the small rear brake fluid reservoir on the right side near the rear footrest
steps.caution: It may sit behind a side cover. Your manual shows where.

steps.say: Squeeze each brake lever, and press the pedal if there is one. Each should firm up, not feel spongy.
steps.target: the front brake lever on the right handlebar

steps.say: The lever should travel only a short way before the brake bites, within the range in your manual.
If the fluid is low or a brake feels spongy or weak, don't ride. Please call a mechanic.

entries.title: Check and clean the battery terminals
entries.meaning: Let's check that your battery terminals are clean and tight.
safety: Switch the ignition off and take out the key.
Keep flames and sparks away. Battery acid burns, so wear safety glasses if you can.

steps.say: Open the battery cover. Your manual shows where, often behind a side panel or under a floor lid.
Look at both terminals. The cables should be tight, with no white crust.
steps.target: the two battery terminals with cables bolted on

steps.say: If they need cleaning, undo the minus cable first, then the plus cable.
steps.target: the negative minus terminal of the battery

steps.say: Clean the terminals and cable ends with a dry cloth, or a small wire brush for heavy crust.
steps.target: the two battery terminals
steps.caution: Keep water out of the battery.

steps.say: Refit the plus cable first, then the minus cable, and tighten both.
steps.target: the positive plus terminal of the battery

steps.say: Smear a thin layer of petroleum jelly over both terminals.
steps.target: the two battery terminals

steps.say: Close the cover. If the battery still seems weak, have it charged or checked by a mechanic.

remind.say: Time to check your bike battery terminals. Make sure they're tight and clean.

entries.title: Check and top up engine oil
entries.meaning: Let's check your engine oil on the dipstick, and top it up if it's low.

steps.say: Find the dipstick. Its handle is a bright ring or loop, usually yellow or orange.
steps.target: the engine oil dipstick handle, a brightly coloured ring or loop, usually yellow or orange
steps.caution: Engine off, and wait about five minutes for the oil to settle. Parts may still be hot.

steps.say: Pull the dipstick all the way out and wipe it clean with a cloth.
steps.target: the engine oil dipstick handle, a brightly coloured ring or loop, usually yellow or orange

steps.say: Push it back in fully, then pull it out again.
steps.target: the engine oil dipstick handle, a brightly coloured ring or loop, usually yellow or orange

steps.say: The oil should be between the two marks near the tip.
steps.target: the end of the oil dipstick with its two level marks

steps.say: If it's near or below the lower mark, unscrew the oil filler cap on top of the engine.
steps.target: the round engine oil filler cap on top of the engine, marked with an oil can symbol or the words engine oil
steps.verify: the engine oil filler cap is off and the round filler opening is visible

steps.say: Slowly pour in a little of the oil your manual recommends.
steps.target: the open round engine oil filler hole on top of the engine
steps.caution: Don't fill above the upper mark. Too much oil is as bad as too little.

steps.say: Screw the filler cap back on tightly, wait a few minutes, then check the dipstick again.
steps.target: the round engine oil filler cap on top of the engine

steps.say: When the oil is between the marks, push the dipstick back in fully.
steps.target: the engine oil dipstick handle, a brightly coloured ring or loop, usually yellow or orange

remind.say: Time for your weekly engine oil check. It only takes a couple of minutes.

entries.source: Maruti Swift OM 99011M75T08-74W p.9-8 + Honda City 2022 OM pp.263, 268-270 + Hyundai Creta 2019 OM p.9-29, 9-30 + Tata Nexon BS-VI OM p.176-177; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Check and top up the engine coolant
entries.meaning: Let's check the coolant in the see-through tank. The engine must be cold.
safety: Only do this when the engine is completely cold.
Never open the radiator cap or coolant cap on a hot engine. Hot coolant can scald you.

steps.say: Open the bonnet and prop it up with its support rod.
Find the see-through plastic coolant tank with level marks on its side.
steps.target: the see-through plastic engine coolant reservoir tank with MIN and MAX or LOW and FULL marks on its side

steps.say: Check the coolant is between the lower and upper marks.
steps.target: the see-through plastic engine coolant reservoir tank with MIN and MAX or LOW and FULL marks on its side

steps.say: If it's below the lower mark, slowly open the tank's cap. Don't open the radiator cap.
steps.target: the cap of the see-through plastic coolant reservoir tank
steps.verify: the coolant reservoir cap is off
steps.caution: Only open it when the engine is cold.

steps.say: Add the coolant type your manual says until it reaches the upper mark.
steps.target: the open see-through plastic coolant reservoir tank
steps.caution: Don't mix different coolant types, and don't fill above the upper mark.

steps.say: Put the cap back on and close it firmly.
steps.target: the cap of the see-through plastic coolant reservoir tank

steps.say: If you need to top up often, please have the cooling system checked for leaks.

remind.say: Time to check your coolant level. Do it with the engine cold.

entries.source: Maruti Swift OM p.9-9, 9-10 + Honda City 2022 OM pp.271-273 + Hyundai Creta 2019 OM pp.9-32 to 9-34 + Tata Nexon BS-VI OM p.178; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Top up windscreen washer fluid
entries.meaning: Let's fill up the windscreen washer fluid.
safety: Switch the engine off and let it cool first. Washer fluid can catch fire on a hot engine.

steps.say: Open the bonnet and prop it up with its support rod.
Find the washer fluid cap. It often shows a windscreen and water spray symbol.
steps.target: the windscreen washer fluid reservoir cap, often blue, with a windscreen and water spray symbol

steps.say: Open the cap.
steps.target: the windscreen washer fluid reservoir cap, often blue, with a windscreen and water spray symbol
steps.verify: the washer fluid cap is open

steps.say: Pour in windscreen washer fluid, mixed with water as the bottle says.
steps.target: the open windscreen washer fluid filler neck
steps.caution: Never put radiator coolant or antifreeze in the washer tank.

steps.say: Stop before it overflows, then close the cap firmly.
steps.target: the windscreen washer fluid reservoir cap

steps.say: If it still doesn't spray once it's full, please have it checked at a workshop.
steps.caution: Don't keep running the washer with an empty tank. It can damage the pump.

remind.say: Quick weekly check: is your windscreen washer tank topped up?

entries.title: Check the battery terminals for corrosion
entries.meaning: Let's look at your battery terminals for corrosion or loose clamps.
safety: Switch the engine off and keep flames, sparks and cigarettes away. Batteries give off explosive gas.
Battery acid burns skin and eyes, so wear eye protection and don't lean over the battery.

steps.say: Open the bonnet and prop it up with its support rod.
Find the battery. It's a box with two metal posts marked plus and minus.
steps.target: the car battery, a rectangular box with two metal terminal posts marked plus and minus

steps.say: Without touching them, look at both posts and clamps for white or yellowish crusty powder.
steps.target: the two battery terminal posts and their cable clamps on top of the car battery
steps.caution: Never let a metal tool touch both posts, or a post and the car body.

steps.say: Check that both cable clamps look tight on their posts.
steps.target: the two battery terminal posts and their cable clamps on top of the car battery

steps.say: If you see powder or a loose clamp, please have a mechanic clean and tighten the terminals.

remind.say: Time for your monthly battery check. Look at the terminals for any white or yellowish crust.

entries.source: Maruti Swift OM p.9-20 + Honda City 2022 OM pp.253, 303-304 + Hyundai Creta 2019 OM pp.9-45 to 9-48 + Tata Nexon BS-VI OM pp.179-181; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Check the brake fluid level
entries.meaning: Let's check the brake fluid level. We'll only look, not top it up.
safety: Park on level ground, set the parking brake and switch the engine off.
Keep the cap closed. Brake fluid harms skin, eyes and paint.

steps.say: Open the bonnet and prop it up with its support rod.
Find the small brake fluid tank, usually at the back of the engine bay on the driver's side.
steps.target: the small see-through brake fluid reservoir with MAX and MIN marks, near the back of the engine bay on the driver's side

steps.say: Without opening it, look at the fluid level through the side of the tank.
steps.target: the small see-through brake fluid reservoir with MAX and MIN marks, near the back of the engine bay on the driver's side

steps.say: The level should be between the MAX and MIN marks.
steps.target: the MAX and MIN marks on the side of the brake fluid reservoir

steps.say: If it's at or near MIN, don't top it up. Please have the brakes checked soon.
steps.caution: If the level drops quickly, there may be a leak. Don't drive until it's checked.

remind.say: Time for your weekly brake fluid check. Just look at the level and keep the cap closed.

entries.source: Maruti Swift OM p.9-13, 9-14 + Honda City 2022 OM pp.253-254, 263, 275 + Hyundai Creta 2019 OM p.9-35, 9-36 + Tata Nexon BS-VI OM p.177; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Check the engine air filter
entries.meaning: Let's open the air filter box and see if the filter is dirty.
safety: Switch the engine off and let it cool before you reach in.

steps.say: Open the bonnet and prop it up with its support rod.
Find the air filter box. It's a large plastic box with clips around its lid.
steps.target: the large plastic engine air filter box with clips around its lid, joined to a wide air intake hose

steps.say: Undo the clips on the lid.
steps.target: the clips on the lid of the engine air filter box

steps.say: Lift the lid and take out the filter.
steps.target: the lid of the engine air filter box
steps.verify: the air filter box lid is open

steps.say: If it looks very dirty or clogged with dust, it needs a new filter of the right type.
steps.target: the engine air filter element

steps.say: Put the filter back the same way, close the lid, and snap all the clips shut.
steps.target: the clips on the lid of the engine air filter box
steps.caution: Don't drive with the filter out, and don't let dirt fall into the box.

remind.say: It's been a while since you looked at your car's air filter. Let's check it.

entries.source: Maruti Swift OM p.9-11 + Hyundai Creta 2019 OM p.9-39; Honda City 2022 lists it for the dealer only; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Car engine won't start
entries.meaning: Let's find out why the car won't start, beginning with the battery and fuel.
symptoms: nothing happens when I turn the key
safety: Set the parking brake firmly. If you're near traffic, turn on the hazard lights.

steps.say: Make sure the gear is in P or neutral, and press the brake or clutch fully.
Switch on the headlights or the inside light, then try to start the engine.
steps.caution: Don't crank for more than about ten seconds at a time.

steps.say: If the lights went very dim or off, the battery is flat or its terminals are loose.
In that case, check the battery terminals look clean and tight.
steps.target: the two battery terminal posts and their cable clamps on top of the car battery

steps.say: If they look fine, the battery needs a jump start or a charge. Just ask me about jump starting.
If the lights stayed bright, check the fuel gauge isn't on empty.
steps.target: the fuel gauge on the instrument cluster

steps.say: If it still won't start, please don't push-start it. Call a mechanic or roadside help.

entries.title: Jump start a flat battery
entries.meaning: Let's jump start your car from another car's battery, connecting the leads in the safe order.
safety: Keep flames, sparks and cigarettes away. Batteries give off explosive gas.
Don't jump start a battery that's cracked, leaking or frozen.

steps.say: Park the other car close, but not touching yours. Both engines off, parking brakes on.
Switch off the AC, music and any lights you don't need.
Clip one end of the first lead to the plus terminal of your flat battery.
steps.target: the plus terminal of the car battery, marked with a plus sign, often under a red cover
steps.caution: Some cars have a separate jump point. Check your manual.

steps.say: Clip the other end of that lead to the plus terminal of the good battery.
Clip the second lead to the minus terminal of the good battery.
Clip its other end to bare, unpainted metal on your engine, such as an engine mounting bolt.
steps.target: a bare unpainted metal bolt on the engine, away from the battery
steps.caution: Never clip it to the minus terminal of the flat battery. It could explode.

steps.say: Start the other car and let it run a little above idle for a few minutes.
steps.caution: Keep hands and leads away from fans and belts.

steps.say: Now start your car.
Remove the leads in the exact reverse order you connected them.
If it won't start after a few tries, or keeps going flat, please call a mechanic.

entries.title: Oil pressure warning light
entries.meaning: The oil light means the oil pressure is low. Let's stop and check the oil.
aliases: oil can light on the dashboard
safety: Pull over somewhere safe and level, and switch the engine off straight away.

steps.say: Wait a few minutes for the oil to settle.
Open the bonnet and prop it up with its support rod.
steps.caution: The engine and the rod may be hot. Hold the rod by its grip.

steps.say: Pull out the dipstick, wipe it, push it back in fully, and pull it out again.
steps.target: the engine oil dipstick handle, a brightly coloured ring or loop, usually yellow or orange

steps.say: If the oil is below the lower mark, add the oil your manual recommends up to the upper mark.
steps.target: the round engine oil filler cap on top of the engine, marked with an oil can symbol or the words engine oil
steps.caution: Don't fill above the upper mark.

steps.say: If the oil level was already fine, don't drive. Please call a workshop.
If you added oil, start the engine. If the light stays on, switch off and call a workshop.
steps.target: the red oil can warning light on the instrument cluster
steps.caution: Running the engine with this light on can badly damage it.

entries.source: Maruti Swift OM p.4-41 + Honda City 2022 OM pp.340-341 + Hyundai Creta 2019 OM p.5-59 + Tata Nexon BS-VI OM p.63; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Engine overheating or temperature warning light
entries.meaning: The engine is running too hot. Let's cool it down safely.
safety: Pull over somewhere safe, park, and switch the AC off.
Don't open the bonnet while steam is coming out, and never open the radiator cap hot.

steps.say: If you see or hear steam, switch the engine off and wait until it stops.
If there's no steam, leave the engine idling for a few minutes to cool down.
steps.target: the temperature warning light or temperature gauge on the instrument cluster

steps.say: Open the bonnet and check the radiator fan is spinning. If not, switch the engine off.
steps.target: the radiator cooling fan behind the radiator at the front of the engine bay
steps.caution: Keep hands and clothes away from the fan and belts. The fan can start by itself.

steps.say: When the temperature is back to normal, switch the engine off and let it cool.
steps.target: the temperature warning light or temperature gauge on the instrument cluster

steps.say: Look for coolant leaking from the radiator, the hoses, or under the car.
steps.target: the radiator and the rubber coolant hoses at the front of the engine bay
steps.caution: Clear water dripping from the AC under the car is normal.

steps.say: If coolant is leaking, don't drive on. Please call a workshop or roadside help.
Once it's cool, check the coolant tank. If it's low, slowly add coolant, never above MAX.
steps.target: the see-through plastic engine coolant reservoir tank with MIN and MAX or LOW and FULL marks on its side
steps.caution: Open only the plastic tank's cap, never the radiator cap.

steps.say: Restart and watch the temperature. If it overheats again, please call a workshop.
steps.target: the temperature warning light or temperature gauge on the instrument cluster

entries.title: Battery charging warning light
entries.meaning: The battery light means the battery isn't being charged. Let's save power and get it checked.
safety: If you need to stop, pull over somewhere safe, away from traffic.

steps.say: It's normal for this light to glow briefly at start-up, then go out.
steps.target: the red battery-shaped warning light on the instrument cluster

steps.say: If it stays on while the engine runs, switch off the AC and anything electrical you don't need.
steps.target: the red battery-shaped warning light on the instrument cluster

steps.say: Please get the charging system checked at a workshop right away. The battery may soon run flat.

entries.title: Check engine light
entries.meaning: The engine light means a fault in the engine or emissions system. Let's see how urgent it is.
safety: If you stop, don't park on dry grass or leaves. A hot exhaust can start a fire.

steps.say: It's normal for the engine light to glow at start-up and go out once the engine runs.
steps.target: the amber engine-shaped warning light on the instrument cluster

steps.say: If it's blinking, slow down and pull over somewhere safe, away from dry grass.
steps.target: the amber engine-shaped warning light on the instrument cluster

steps.say: Switch the engine off and let it cool for a while.
If you must move the car, drive slowly and gently straight to a workshop.
If the light is steady, not blinking, avoid high speeds and get the engine checked soon.
steps.target: the amber engine-shaped warning light on the instrument cluster

entries.title: Brake warning light
entries.meaning: The red brake light means the parking brake is on, brake fluid is low, or a brake fault.
symptoms: parking brake light won't go off
safety: If it came on while driving, slow down gently and stop somewhere safe. You may need to brake harder.

steps.say: First, make sure the parking brake is fully released.
steps.target: the parking brake lever or button next to the driver's seat

steps.say: If the light stays on with the parking brake off, the brake fluid may be low.
steps.target: the red brake warning light on the instrument cluster, often a circle with an exclamation mark or the word BRAKE

steps.say: With the engine off, open the bonnet and look at the brake fluid tank's level.
steps.target: the small see-through brake fluid reservoir with MAX and MIN marks, near the back of the engine bay on the driver's side

steps.say: If it's at or below MIN, it isn't safe to drive. Please call a workshop or roadside help.
If the level looks fine but the light stays on, please have the brakes checked right away.
steps.caution: If the brake light and the ABS light are both on, get it checked immediately.

entries.title: Inverter giving no backup or short backup
entries.meaning: Let's find out why your inverter backup is short or not working.
symptoms: lights go off in a power cut
aliases: UPS not working in power cut
safety: Don't open the inverter's cover. There's high voltage inside, even when it's switched off.

steps.say: Check the inverter's front switch is on, and its plug is firmly in a working socket.
steps.target: the power switch on the front panel of the inverter

steps.say: Look at the small breaker on the back. If it has tripped, switch it back on once.
steps.target: the small circuit breaker switch or button on the back of the inverter
steps.caution: If it trips again, leave it and call a technician.

steps.say: In a power cut, switch off heavy appliances you don't need. Too much load drains the battery fast.
After a long power cut, let the battery recharge on mains power for several hours.
If your battery has water level indicators on top, switch the inverter off and unplug it first.
steps.target: the water level indicators on top of the inverter battery
steps.caution: Sealed maintenance-free batteries don't need water.

steps.say: Check the indicators. If any shows low, top up slowly with distilled water, only to the max mark.
steps.target: the water level indicators on top of the inverter battery
steps.caution: Wear gloves; battery acid burns. Never use tap or drinking water, and keep flames away.

steps.say: Close the caps firmly, wipe any spills, then plug the inverter back in and switch it on.
steps.target: the vent caps on top of the inverter battery

steps.say: If backup is still short, the battery may be worn out. Please call a technician.

entries.source: Microtek Heavy Duty VTurbo SW UPS OM p.3-4, 6-7 + Livfast Smart Flash UPS OM p.2-3, 5, 8-9 + Luminous battery water and maintenance guides (luminousindia.com) + Genus battery top-up guide + Livguard LGS1100i product FAQ; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Inverter beeping or showing overload
entries.meaning: Let's find out why the inverter is beeping.
safety: Don't open the inverter's cover. There's high voltage inside, even when it's switched off.

steps.say: Look at the inverter's display or lights. They show whether it's overload or battery low.
steps.target: the display and indicator lights on the front of the inverter

steps.say: For overload, switch off heavy appliances until the warning stops.
Then reset it: switch the inverter off at its front switch, and back on.
steps.target: the power switch on the front panel of the inverter

steps.say: For battery low in a power cut, switch off what you don't need. It recharges when power returns.
If it keeps beeping with little load, or shows a fault or short circuit, please call a technician.

entries.meaning: Don't touch the battery. If it's safe, switch the inverter off and unplug it, then call a technician.

entries.title: Open a laptop's bottom cover for cleaning
entries.meaning: Let's take the bottom cover off so you can clean the dust out.
aliases: open the back of the laptop
safety: Shut the laptop down fully, unplug the charger, and remove any cables and cards.
Work on a clean, flat, dry table, and touch bare metal first to discharge static.

steps.say: Check your laptop's manual first; on many models, opening the cover can void the warranty.
Close the lid and turn the laptop upside down on the table.
steps.target: the bottom cover of the laptop

steps.say: Remove every screw from the bottom cover, and keep track of where each one goes.
steps.target: the small screws around the edge of the laptop's bottom cover
steps.caution: Some screws stay in the cover, and some hide under rubber feet. Check your manual.

steps.say: Gently pry the cover loose with a plastic pry tool, working around the edge.
steps.target: the seam along the edge of the laptop's bottom cover
steps.caution: Don't force it; clips broken by force aren't covered by warranty.

steps.say: Lift the cover off and set it aside.
steps.target: the laptop's bottom cover
steps.verify: the laptop bottom cover is lifted off

steps.say: Unplug the battery cable from the board by pulling its connector, never the wires.
steps.target: the battery cable connector where the flat battery's wires plug into the circuit board
steps.caution: If the battery looks swollen or puffed up, stop and call a technician.

steps.say: Blow the dust out of the fan and vents with short puffs of compressed air.
steps.target: the round cooling fan and the metal fins next to it
steps.caution: Hold the fan still and the can upright. Don't use a vacuum cleaner.

steps.say: Plug the battery cable back in until it sits fully in its socket.
steps.target: the battery cable connector on the circuit board

steps.say: Snap the cover back on and put every screw back in its own hole.
steps.target: the bottom cover of the laptop
steps.caution: Make sure no screw is left loose inside before you switch it on.

entries.source: Dell Inspiron 15 3520 Service Manual (2023): before working inside, safety, removing/installing the base cover, swollen batteries; HP 15 Laptop PC Maintenance and Service Guide (L58964-001): preparation, bottom cover; Lenovo IdeaPad Gaming 3 HMM (2022): general guidelines, remove the lower case, battery; Dell blog 'How to clean a laptop fan safely'; HP Tech Takes 'How to clean your laptop'; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Laptop not charging
entries.meaning: Let's find out why the laptop isn't charging.
safety: If the charger or its cable is damaged or buzzing, unplug it and don't use it.

steps.say: Unplug the charger from both the wall socket and the laptop.
steps.target: the charger plug in the side of the laptop

steps.say: Check the cable and plugs for fraying, kinks, or bent pins.
steps.target: the laptop charger's cable and power brick
steps.caution: If anything is damaged, stop and get a replacement charger from the maker.

steps.say: Look inside the laptop's charging port for dust or lint, and gently clear it.
steps.target: the charging port on the side of the laptop

steps.say: Plug the charger firmly into the laptop, then into a wall socket you know works.
steps.target: the charging port on the side of the laptop
steps.caution: On USB-C laptops, only some ports can charge. Check your manual.

steps.say: Check that the charging light next to the charging port comes on.
steps.target: the small charging light next to the laptop's charging port
steps.caution: Where the light is differs by model.

steps.say: If it stops at sixty or eighty percent, a battery-saving setting may be on; check the maker's app.
steps.caution: Stopping just short of full is normal; it protects the battery.

steps.say: If it still won't charge, please call a technician.

entries.title: Laptop overheating or fan too loud
entries.meaning: Let's find out why the laptop is running hot.
safety: If it's too hot to hold, shut it down, unplug it, and let it cool.

steps.say: Put the laptop on a hard, flat table, not a bed, sofa, cushion, or your lap.
Make sure nothing is covering the air vents on the sides, back, or bottom.
steps.target: the slotted air vents on the side or back edge of the laptop

steps.say: Close programs you aren't using; Task Manager shows which ones work hardest.
Shut it down and unplug the charger before cleaning the vents.
Blow short puffs of compressed air into the vents to clear the dust.
steps.target: the slotted air vents on the side or back edge of the laptop
steps.caution: Hold the can upright, and don't use a vacuum or an air compressor.

steps.say: If it still runs hot, the fan may need cleaning inside; please call a technician.

entries.title: Laptop battery swollen
entries.meaning: Please stop using the laptop and unplug the charger. Don't press, puncture, or try to remove a swollen battery.
safety: Stop using it and unplug the charger; don't charge a swollen battery.
Don't press, bend, puncture, or pry the battery, and keep it away from heat.

entries.title: Microwave not starting or not heating
entries.meaning: Let's find out why the microwave won't start or heat.
symptoms: nothing happens when I press start
safety: Never open the microwave's outer casing. There's high voltage inside.

steps.say: Check the plug is pushed fully into the socket and the socket switch is on.
steps.target: the microwave's power plug in the wall socket

steps.say: Check the breaker or fuse for that socket hasn't tripped. Test the socket with another appliance.
steps.caution: If the breaker keeps tripping, call an electrician.

steps.say: Wipe any food off the door edges, then close the door firmly.
steps.target: the edge of the microwave door and the front frame where it closes

steps.say: If the display shows a lock sign, child lock is on. Check your manual to unlock it.
steps.target: the display on the microwave's control panel

steps.say: Set a cooking time, then press Start.
steps.target: the Start button on the microwave's control panel
steps.caution: Never run it empty. Always put food inside first.

steps.say: If it still won't start or heat, please call a technician. Don't try to repair it.

entries.title: Sparks or arcing inside the microwave
entries.meaning: Sparks usually mean there's metal inside. Let's stop it and find the cause.
safety: Press Stop straight away.
If you see smoke or flames, keep the door shut and unplug the microwave.

steps.say: Take out any foil, metal spoon, twist tie or metal container.
steps.target: the inside of the microwave oven
steps.caution: The dish and food may be hot. Use oven gloves.

steps.say: Don't use plates or cups with a gold or silver rim or a painted pattern.
Check the glass tray and its roller ring are sitting properly in place.
steps.target: the round glass turntable tray inside the microwave

steps.say: Never run the microwave empty. There should always be food inside.
If it still sparks with nothing metal inside, stop using it and call a technician.

entries.meaning: Please stop using it. Keep the door shut, unplug it, and call a technician. Never open the casing.

entries.title: Fridge not cooling
entries.meaning: Let's find out why your fridge isn't cooling properly.
aliases: milk going bad in the fridge
safety: Don't open or unscrew any cover at the back of the fridge. There are gas pipes behind it.

steps.say: Check the fridge is plugged in firmly and the wall switch is on.
steps.target: the fridge's power plug in the wall socket

steps.say: If the inside light and display stay off, test that socket with another appliance.
Turn the temperature knob one step colder, or set the fridge to about three degrees.
steps.target: the temperature control knob or display of the fridge

steps.say: If it was just switched on or loaded with food, give it a few hours to cool.
Make sure the door shuts fully, with no shelf, drawer or bottle stopping it.
steps.target: the edge of the fridge door where it meets the cabinet

steps.say: Wipe the rubber door seal clean with a damp cloth so it seals tightly.
steps.target: the rubber door seal around the edge of the fridge door
steps.caution: If the seal is torn or leaves a gap, it needs replacing.

steps.say: Don't overpack it. Leave gaps between the food so cold air can flow.
Move any food that's blocking the cold air vents inside.
steps.target: the cold air vent slots on the back wall inside the fridge

steps.say: Leave about a hand's width of space between the fridge and the walls behind and beside it.
Keep it out of direct sun and away from the stove or other heat.
Unplug it, vacuum the dust off the grille at the lower back, then plug it back in.
steps.target: the ventilation grille at the lower back of the fridge
steps.caution: Only clean the outside. Don't remove any cover.

steps.say: If it's still not cold after a few hours, please call a technician.

entries.title: Water inside or under the fridge
entries.meaning: Let's find out where the water in your fridge is coming from.
symptoms: water on the floor near the fridge
water at the bottom of the fridge
safety: If water is near the plug or socket, switch off at the wall before you touch anything.

steps.say: A few drops inside after the door's been open are normal. Bigger puddles are what we're fixing.
Make sure the door closes fully every time, so warm damp air can't get in.
steps.target: the edge of the fridge door where it meets the cabinet

steps.say: Let hot food cool to room temperature before you put it in.
Keep food and drinks covered or in closed containers, so nothing spills.
Look for the small drain hole or channel on the back wall inside, and clear any food bits.
steps.target: the small drain hole or channel on the back wall inside the fridge compartment
steps.caution: Don't pour hot water into it.

steps.say: If there's a drip tray under the freezer box, empty it and set it back straight.
steps.target: the plastic drip tray under the freezer box

steps.say: In a single door fridge, defrost every few days so melting ice doesn't overflow.
If water still collects, please unplug the fridge and call a technician.

entries.source: LG India help library (water on the floor; top-freezer water leak) + Samsung India water leakage in refrigerator page + Godrej direct cool user manual p.5, 8, 9 + LG India direct cool defrost page; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Too much ice or frost in the fridge
entries.meaning: Let's clear the extra ice and stop it building up again.
safety: Never chip the ice with a knife or anything sharp. It can damage the fridge.

steps.say: Make sure the fridge door and the freezer door close fully, with nothing sticking out.
steps.target: the freezer door

steps.say: Wipe the rubber door seal clean, and check it isn't torn or loose.
steps.target: the rubber door seal around the edge of the fridge door

steps.say: If your fridge has a defrost button, take the food out of the freezer box first.
steps.target: the freezer box at the top inside the fridge

steps.say: Check the drip tray is in place under the freezer box to catch the water.
steps.target: the plastic drip tray under the freezer box

steps.say: Press the defrost button, usually in the middle of the temperature knob.
steps.target: the defrost button in the centre of the round temperature knob inside the fridge
steps.caution: On some models the button is inside the freezer box.

steps.say: Keep the door closed. When the ice has melted, the button pops out and cooling restarts.
From now on, let hot food cool before it goes in, and open the door less often.
Defrost every few days, before the ice gets thicker than about half a centimetre.
If a fridge without a defrost button keeps icing up, or the button won't pop out, call a technician.

entries.title: Noisy fridge
entries.meaning: Let's find out what's making the noise. Many fridge sounds are normal.
safety: Unplug the fridge before you move it or turn its feet.

steps.say: Soft humming, gurgling, cracking, or a click when the motor starts or stops is normal.
A new fridge, or one that was just moved or switched on, runs louder at first.
Take anything off the top of the fridge.
steps.target: the top surface of the fridge

steps.say: Pull the fridge slightly out so its back and sides don't touch the wall or cabinets.
Check it stands firm. If it rocks, turn the front feet until it's level and steady.
steps.target: the adjustable levelling feet at the bottom front corners of the fridge

steps.say: Make sure no food or ice is pressing against the fan at the back of the freezer.
steps.target: the fan cover on the back wall inside the freezer

steps.say: Wait about ten minutes, then plug the fridge back in and listen again.
steps.target: the fridge's power plug in the wall socket

steps.say: If it still grinds, bangs or rattles loudly, please call a technician.

entries.meaning: This needs a trained technician. If you smell burning or see smoke, unplug the fridge now.

entries.title: TV won't turn on
entries.meaning: Let's find out why the TV won't turn on.
symptoms: nothing happens when I press power
safety: Keep your hands dry, and pull plugs out by the plug, never by the cord.

steps.say: Look at the small standby light on the TV's bottom edge. Is it on, off, or blinking?
steps.target: the small standby light on the bottom edge of the TV, usually under the logo
steps.caution: A blinking light usually means a fault inside the TV.

steps.say: Press the power button on the TV itself, not on the remote.
steps.target: the power button on the TV, usually under the logo at the bottom edge
steps.caution: On some models it's on the back or side. If the TV turns on, the remote is the problem.

steps.say: Push the power cord firmly into the back of the TV and into the wall socket.
steps.target: the power cord where it plugs into the back of the TV
steps.caution: If the cord is cut, crushed or scorched, don't plug it in.

steps.say: Plug a lamp or phone charger into the same socket to check the socket works.
steps.target: the wall socket the TV is plugged into
steps.caution: If the TV is on a power strip or extension, plug it straight into the wall.

steps.say: Unplug the TV, wait two minutes, then plug it back in and press power.
steps.caution: After plugging in, give it up to twenty seconds to start.

steps.say: If the standby light stays off or keeps blinking, please call a technician.

entries.title: TV has sound but no picture
entries.meaning: Let's find out why you can hear the TV but the screen stays black.
symptoms: can hear it but can't see anything
safety: Never open the back of the TV; there's dangerous voltage inside.
Switch off the TV and the set-top box before you unplug or plug in any cable.

steps.say: Press Home or Menu on the remote. If a menu appears, the screen itself is working.
steps.target: the Home or Menu button on the TV remote
steps.caution: A picture-off or screen-off setting also wakes up when you press a button.

steps.say: Press Input or Source on the remote and pick the input your set-top box uses.
steps.target: the Input or Source button on the TV remote

steps.say: Make sure the set-top box or other device is switched on.
steps.target: the set-top box or device connected to the TV

steps.say: With both switched off, pull out the HDMI cable at both ends and push it back firmly.
steps.target: the HDMI cable plugged into the back or side of the TV
steps.caution: If you have a spare HDMI cable or a free HDMI socket, try that too.

steps.say: Unplug the TV and the set-top box for a minute, then plug both back in.
If no menu ever appears, or the picture stays black, please call a technician.

entries.title: TV shows no signal
entries.meaning: Let's get a signal back to your TV.
safety: Switch off the TV and the set-top box before you unplug or plug in any cable.

steps.say: Press Input or Source on the remote and choose the input your device is plugged into.
steps.target: the Input or Source button on the TV remote
steps.caution: If the box is in the HDMI 1 socket, choose HDMI 1.

steps.say: Make sure the set-top box or other device is switched on.
steps.target: the set-top box or device connected to the TV

steps.say: With both switched off, pull out the HDMI cable at both ends and push it back firmly.
steps.target: the HDMI cable plugged into the back or side of the TV
steps.caution: Try another HDMI socket or a spare cable too, then pick that input.

steps.say: If you use an antenna or cable wire, push it firmly into its socket on the TV.
steps.target: the round antenna or cable socket on the back of the TV

steps.say: Switch the set-top box off at the wall for thirty seconds, then back on.
steps.target: the set-top box connected to the TV
steps.caution: Give the box a minute or two to start up.

steps.say: If it still says no signal, please call your set-top box provider or a technician.

entries.title: TV remote not working
entries.meaning: Let's find out why the remote isn't working.
symptoms: buttons on the remote don't work
safety: Keep batteries away from small children, and don't mix old and new ones.

steps.say: Press the power button on the TV itself to check the TV is working.
steps.target: the power button on the TV, usually under the logo at the bottom edge
steps.caution: On some models it's on the back or side.

steps.say: Move anything blocking the space between the remote and the front of the TV.
steps.target: the remote sensor window on the bottom front edge of the TV
steps.caution: A soundbar in front of the TV can block the sensor.

steps.say: Take out the batteries, hold the remote's power button for eight seconds, then fit new ones.
steps.target: the battery cover on the back of the TV remote
steps.caution: Match the plus and minus marks inside the cover.

steps.say: Point the remote straight at the bottom front of the TV and press power.
steps.target: the remote sensor window on the bottom front edge of the TV

steps.say: Point the remote at this phone's camera and press a button. Look for a flashing light at its tip.
steps.target: the small dark window at the front tip of the TV remote
steps.caution: This camera test doesn't work on every phone.

steps.say: No flashing light means the remote needs replacing. If it flashes but the TV ignores it, please call a technician.

entries.title: TV damaged, smoking or showing lines
entries.meaning: Please don't open the TV's back; there's dangerous voltage inside. If you see smoke or smell burning, unplug it.
aliases: open the back of the tv
safety: Unplug the TV right away if you see smoke or sparks, or smell burning.
Don't open the back cover; there are no parts inside you can fix yourself.

entries.title: Washing machine not draining
entries.meaning: Let's find out why the water isn't draining.
safety: Switch the machine off and unplug it.
If it just ran a hot wash, let the water cool for about an hour first.

steps.say: Check the drain hose behind the machine isn't bent, squashed or blocked.
steps.target: the ribbed drain hose coming out of the back of the washing machine

steps.say: Check the end of the drain hose sits in the drain the way your manual shows.
steps.target: the end of the drain hose where it goes into the drain pipe or floor outlet
steps.caution: The right height differs by model.

steps.say: On a front-loader, open the small flap at the bottom front. No flap? Say next until the last step.
steps.target: the small square flap at the bottom front corner of the washing machine
steps.verify: the small flap at the bottom front corner of the washing machine is open
steps.caution: Some flaps need a coin to open.

steps.say: Put a wide, shallow tray and an old towel on the floor below the flap.
Pull out the small drain tube, open its cap, and let the water run into the tray.
steps.target: the small drain tube with a cap behind the bottom front flap
steps.caution: There can be a lot of water. Cap the tube to empty the tray.

steps.say: When it stops, cap the tube and slowly unscrew the round filter anticlockwise.
steps.target: the round filter cap with a grip handle behind the bottom front flap
steps.caution: A little more water will come out.

steps.say: Clear out lint, coins and hair, and rinse the filter under the tap.
Check the opening is clear and the small propeller inside it can turn.
steps.target: the round opening behind the filter at the bottom front of the washing machine

steps.say: Screw the filter back in firmly, clockwise, and close the flap.
steps.target: the round filter opening behind the bottom front flap
steps.caution: A loose filter will leak.

steps.say: Plug it in and run a spin-only or drain cycle. If it still won't drain, please call a technician.
steps.caution: Watch the filter for drips.

entries.source: Samsung WW70T4020EE manual pp.10,45,48,51-52,55 + Samsung India 4E/5E page + LG help library OE (UAE) and drain pump filter (US) + Bosch India E18 page + IFB Senator Plus manual pp.60,67,75 + Whirlpool product help F9E1 and drain pump filter; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Washing machine not filling with water
entries.meaning: Let's find out why water isn't coming into the machine.
safety: Switch the machine off and unplug it before touching the hoses.

steps.say: Make sure the water tap feeding the machine is turned fully on.
steps.target: the water tap on the wall that the washing machine's inlet hose is connected to

steps.say: Check other taps in the house have water. If the supply's off, wait for it to return.
Follow the inlet hose from the tap to the machine and straighten any kinks.
steps.target: the inlet water hose running from the tap to the back of the washing machine

steps.say: Shut the door, or the lid on a top-loader, firmly. Many machines won't fill with it open.
steps.target: the washing machine door

steps.say: Turn the tap off, then unscrew the inlet hose from the back of the machine.
steps.target: the point where the inlet hose screws onto the back of the washing machine
steps.caution: Hold a cloth over it; a little water will come out.

steps.say: Gently pull out the small mesh filter with pliers and rinse it clean under the tap.
steps.target: the water inlet connector on the back of the washing machine
steps.caution: It sits in the machine's inlet or in the hose end, depending on the model.

steps.say: Push the filter back in, screw the hose on, and open the tap. Check for drips.
steps.target: the point where the inlet hose screws onto the back of the washing machine

steps.say: Plug it in and start the cycle again. If it still won't fill, please call a technician.

entries.source: Samsung WW70T4020EE manual pp.47,51,55 + Samsung India 4E/5E page + LG help library IE (UAE) + Bosch India E17 page + IFB Senator Plus manual pp.59,65,74 + Whirlpool product help F8E1; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Door won't open, close or lock
entries.meaning: Let's get the door working. It stays locked on purpose while the machine is hot, full or spinning.
safety: Never force the door. The water and clothes inside can be very hot.

steps.say: If a cycle is running, press Start/Pause and wait for the drum to stop.
steps.target: the Start/Pause button on the washing machine control panel

steps.say: If the door's locked shut, wait a few minutes for it to click open by itself.
steps.target: the door lock symbol on the washing machine control panel
steps.caution: After a hot wash or a power cut it can take longer.

steps.say: If Child Lock is on, turn it off. It's often two buttons held for three seconds.
steps.target: the child lock symbol on the washing machine control panel
steps.caution: Your manual shows which buttons.

steps.say: If water is still inside, run a drain or spin-only cycle, then wait for the lock.
Once it's open, check no clothes are caught in the rubber seal, or under a top-loader's lid.
steps.target: the rubber seal around the door opening of the washing machine

steps.say: Look at the door hook and its catch. If either is bent or broken, please call a technician.
steps.target: the hook on the inside edge of the washing machine door

steps.say: Push the door firmly shut until it clicks.
steps.target: the washing machine door

steps.say: Switch it off at the wall for a few minutes, then switch on and try again.
If the door still won't open or lock, please call a technician. Never force it.

entries.source: Samsung WW70T4020EE manual pp.8-9,42,52,55-56 + Samsung US error-code page + LG help library dE (UAE), door won't open (UK) and locked door (Canada) + Bosch India E16 page + IFB Senator Plus manual pp.16,39-40,64,73 + Whirlpool product help F5E2/LdL; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Shaking or unbalanced load
entries.meaning: Let's calm the shaking. It's usually an uneven load or a machine that isn't level.
safety: Pause the machine and wait until the drum has stopped completely.

steps.say: Open the door or lid and spread the clothes evenly around the drum, untangling any knots.
steps.target: the clothes inside the washing machine drum

steps.say: If it's one heavy item, like jeans or a blanket, add a few towels to balance it.
If the drum is packed tight, take a few things out.
steps.target: the clothes inside the washing machine drum

steps.say: Close the door or lid and start the spin again.
Check the machine doesn't rock. If it does, adjust the feet so all four sit firmly.
steps.target: the adjustable feet at the bottom corners of the washing machine
steps.caution: Your manual shows how to lock the feet afterwards.

steps.say: Make sure it stands on a solid, level floor, not on a carpet or rug.
New machine? Check the transit bolts on the back were taken out. If not, your manual shows how.
steps.target: the transit bolts or round plastic caps on the back panel of the washing machine

steps.say: If it still shakes hard or moves across the floor, please call a technician.

entries.source: Samsung WW70T4020EE manual pp.18,21,51-52 + Samsung US error-code page + LG help library UE (UAE) + IFB Senator Plus manual pp.13,16,21-22,67-68,76 + Whirlpool product help OFb/OL and F7E1; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Washing machine won't start
entries.meaning: Let's find out why it won't start, beginning with the power.
safety: Keep your hands dry when you touch the plug, socket or switches.

steps.say: Check it's plugged straight into a wall socket, not an extension cord, and the switch is on.
steps.target: the washing machine's power plug and the wall socket switch

steps.say: Plug a lamp or phone charger into that socket to see if it has power.
steps.target: the wall socket the washing machine plugs into

steps.say: If the socket's dead, check your home's MCB or fuse box for a tripped switch.
steps.caution: If it trips again, call an electrician.

steps.say: Close the door, or the lid on a top-loader, firmly until it clicks.
steps.target: the washing machine door

steps.say: Make sure the water tap is turned on.
steps.target: the water tap on the wall that the washing machine's inlet hose is connected to

steps.say: If the buttons don't respond, Child Lock may be on. Hold its buttons for about three seconds.
steps.target: the child lock symbol on the washing machine control panel
steps.caution: Your manual shows which buttons.

steps.say: Choose a program, then press Start/Pause.
steps.target: the Start/Pause button on the washing machine control panel

steps.say: Check the display isn't counting down a delay start or paused in a soak.
steps.target: the display on the washing machine control panel

steps.say: If the display stays dark or it still won't start, please call a technician.

entries.source: Samsung WW70T4020EE manual pp.8-9,42,51,53,56 + Samsung US error-code page + LG help library CL/PF (UAE) and power-on page (US) + IFB Senator Plus manual pp.15,39,64-65,70,73 + Whirlpool product help LOC/PF; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Bad smell or dirty drum
entries.meaning: Let's freshen it up. Musty smells usually come from leftover detergent and damp inside.
symptoms: black gunk in the rubber seal
safety: Switch the machine off and unplug it before you clean inside.

steps.say: Take everything out of the drum. The cleaning program has to run empty.
steps.target: the inside of the washing machine drum

steps.say: On a front-loader, wipe the rubber door seal with a damp cloth, including inside its folds.
steps.target: the rubber seal around the door opening of the washing machine
steps.caution: Pick out any hair, coins or fluff you find.

steps.say: Slide out the detergent drawer and rinse it under warm running water with a soft brush.
steps.target: the detergent drawer on the front of the washing machine
steps.caution: Your manual shows how it releases; some have a small lever.

steps.say: Wipe out the drawer's slot too, then slide the drawer back in.
steps.target: the empty detergent drawer slot on the front of the washing machine

steps.say: Plug in and run the drum clean or tub clean program with the drum empty.
steps.target: the program dial or program buttons on the washing machine control panel
steps.caution: Its name differs by model; check your manual.

steps.say: From now on, use only the detergent amount on the pack. Extra suds leave smelly residue.
After each wash, leave the door slightly open so the inside can dry.
If it still smells after a clean cycle, please call a technician.

remind.say: Time for your monthly drum clean. Run it with the drum empty.

entries.source: Samsung WW70T4020EE manual pp.12,43,49,54 + LG help library tcL/Sud (UAE) + IFB Senator Plus manual pp.13,58,61,66 + Whirlpool product help odours, door seal and HE detergent pages; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Fault that needs a technician
entries.meaning: That's a fault inside the machine. With dry hands, switch it off at the wall and turn off its tap.
entries.source: Samsung WW70T4020EE manual pp.8,55-56 + LG help library CE/PE/tE/SE/FE/dHE (UAE) + Bosch India E19-E28 pages; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Geyser not giving hot water
entries.meaning: Let's find out why the geyser isn't giving you hot water.
aliases: geyser takes too long to heat
safety: Don't open the geyser's cover or touch its wiring. We'll only use the switch, the knob and the valve.

steps.say: Check the geyser's switch on the wall is turned on.
steps.target: the wall switch next to the socket the geyser is plugged into

steps.say: Look for the power light on the geyser. It should glow when the switch is on.
steps.target: the small indicator lights on the front of the geyser

steps.say: If no light glows at all, don't try to reset anything. Please call a technician.
Check the valve on the cold water pipe going into the geyser is fully open.
steps.target: the valve handle on the cold water pipe going into the bottom of the geyser

steps.say: If your geyser has a temperature knob, turn it clockwise to a warmer setting.
steps.target: the round temperature knob on the front of the geyser
steps.caution: Only use the outside knob, and don't force it past its last mark.

steps.say: Now give it half an hour to an hour to heat up before you use it.
If there's still no hot water, or the switch keeps tripping, please call a technician.

entries.source: V-Guard Divino OM p.5, 7 + A. O. Smith Finesse SDS OM p.10-11, 13 + Racold CDR/Buono Pro OM p.3, 8, 13 + Racold Eterno 2 NXT OM p.5 + Havells Adonia R OM p.12, 14 + Havells Monza Slim i OM p.31; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Geyser leaking or dripping water
entries.meaning: Let's see where the water is coming from, and whether it's normal.
symptoms: drops from the pipe under the geyser
aliases: water coming out of the geyser
safety: Switch the geyser off at the wall. If that switch is wet, use the main switch instead.

steps.say: Look where the water comes from: the small valve under the geyser, a pipe joint, or the tank.
steps.target: the pipes and valve under the bottom of the geyser

steps.say: A few drops from the safety valve while it heats are normal. Water expands as it warms.
steps.target: the safety valve with a small lever on the cold water pipe under the geyser

steps.say: Never block, plug or tighten that valve to stop the drips. It protects the tank.
If it drips all the time, not just while heating, the pressure may be high. Please call a plumber.
If water leaks from the tank or its joints, keep the geyser off and call a technician.

entries.meaning: That isn't safe to fix yourself. Switch the geyser off at the main switch and call a technician.

entries.title: Gas geyser smells of gas or burns badly
entries.meaning: Close the gas valve, open windows, put out flames, and don't touch switches. Then call a technician.
symptoms: smell of gas in the bathroom
flame stays on after tap is closed

entries.title: Water purifier giving no water or a slow flow
entries.meaning: Let's find out why the purifier isn't giving you enough water.
safety: Don't open the purifier's cover or pull out its filters yourself.

steps.say: Check the purifier is switched on at the wall and its power light is glowing.
steps.target: the power indicator light on the front of the water purifier

steps.say: Make sure the tap that feeds it has water, and the overhead tank isn't empty.
Check the small valve on the pipe going into the purifier is fully open.
steps.target: the small valve with a lever on the thin pipe going into the water purifier

steps.say: Low supply pressure or heavy use makes it slow. Give the tank time to refill.
If a filter change light is on or blinking, the filters are due. Please book a service.
steps.target: the indicator lights on the front panel of the water purifier

steps.say: If there's still little or no water, please call a technician.

entries.source: A. O. Smith Z5 RO OM p.11-12 + Aquaguard Delight NXT OM p.7-8 + Livpure Pep OM p.15-17 + KENT Grand OM p.3, 5-6, 12 + KENT Maxx OM p.5-6; checked 2026-09-27

entries.title: Purified water tastes or smells bad
entries.meaning: Let's work out why the water tastes or smells odd.
safety: Don't drink the water while it tastes or smells wrong.
Don't open the purifier or change its filters yourself.

steps.say: If the water sat in the tank for over two days, drain it out through the tap.
steps.target: the dispensing tap on the front of the water purifier

steps.say: Let it refill with fresh water, then taste it again.
If the filter change light is on, the filters are due. Please book a service.
steps.target: the indicator lights on the front panel of the water purifier

steps.say: If it still tastes or smells odd, don't drink it. Please call a technician.

entries.title: Water purifier leaking
entries.meaning: Let's stop the leak safely first, then see where it's coming from.
symptoms: water on the floor under the purifier
water coming out of the top of the purifier
safety: Close the small valve on the pipe that feeds the purifier.
Switch the purifier off at the wall and unplug it. If the socket is wet, use the main switch.

steps.say: Wipe the area dry, then look for a loose pipe or tap joint you can see from outside.
steps.target: the pipe connections and the tap on the outside of the water purifier

steps.say: Don't open the cover or pull pipes apart to fix it yourself.
Leave it off with the valve closed, and call a technician to fix the leak.
